title: Leaking Heap Data for Static Lifetimes
goal: Convert a heap allocation into a `'static` reference with `Box::leak`.

sections.text: Rust references with a `'static` lifetime live for the entire duration of the program. String literals like `"hello"` have `'static` lifetime because they are stored in the compiled binary.

sections.caption: String literals are embedded in binary.

sections.text: Sometimes you construct data dynamically at runtime. You may need `'static` references to it without keeping an owning variable.
`Box::leak` takes ownership of a `Box<T>`. It skips running the destructor and returns a `&'static mut T` reference.

sections.caption: Box::leak turns heap memory into static.

sections.text: The heap allocation is never reclaimed. Use `Box::leak` intentionally for program-wide values initialized once at startup.

explanation: Convert a heap allocation into a `'static` reference with `Box::leak`.
